title: 매일 아침 보게 될 시청률표  (The Morning Ratings Sheet)

segments.t: Walking the rookies through the open variety floor, Kim Tae-ho shows them the daily ratings printout and demonstrates how to fend off friends asking for Gag Concert studio tickets. Listen for the phrases for 'ratings chart' and 'there aren't any'.
이게 매일 아침 보게 될 시청률표야.
이게 우리한테는 성적표 같은 거지.
요새 칠 나오기 쉽지가 않아요.
되게 기대를 많이 하고 왔단 말이에요.
가끔 혼란이 오더라고요.
다들 내가 하는 거 잘 봐.
이번 주 개콘표? 없어요.
처음부터 안 된다고 선을 그어놓는 게 좋아.
Let's break down those eight lines from the variety office tour.
이게 매일 아침 보게 될 시청률표야.

It literally means this. 'This is the ratings chart you'll see every morning.' The phrase for 'every morning' pairs 'every day' with 'morning', a time chunk you can drop into any daily routine. The word for 'ratings chart' tacks the suffix for 'chart' or 'table' onto the word for television viewership ratings Swap in this word.
이게 우리한테는 성적표 같은 거지.

It literally means this. 'For us, this is like a report card.' Adding a topic word onto the word for 'us' means 'as far as we are concerned'. He compares the numbers to a school report card, followed by a phrase meaning 'it is something like' This means that.
요새 칠 나오기 쉽지가 않아요.

It literally means this. 'Getting a seven isn't easy these days.' He uses the breezy spoken cousin of the standard word for 'these days'. Seven percent is stated as a sino-korean number, and the word ending flips 'easy' into 'not easy at all' This literally means that.
되게 기대를 많이 하고 왔단 말이에요.

It literally means this. 'I came here with really high expectations.' Cutting to his interview, Seung-chan pairs an word meaning 'really' or 'super' with the expression for 'to have big expectations'. The sentence ending adds an earnest 'I mean, really!' tone This short for that.
가끔 혼란이 오더라고요.

It literally means this. 'Sometimes I get confused.' Korean says confusion comes to you, literally phrasing it as 'confusion came'. The word at the front means 'sometimes' or 'every now and then' It is a handy word.
다들 내가 하는 거 잘 봐.

It literally means this. 'Everyone, watch closely what I do.' Back at his desk, Tae-ho gathers the rookies with the word for 'everyone'. His command pairs the word for 'well' or 'closely' with the casual word 'look!' We built from this.
이번 주 개콘표? 없어요.

It literally means this. 'This week's Gag Concert tickets? We don't have any.' Notice how the same word that meant 'chart' earlier means an admission 'ticket' for Gag Concert here! His one-word answer — 'there are none' — works in shops, offices, and cafés alike The word doubles the.
처음부터 안 된다고 선을 그어놓는 게 좋아.

It literally means this. 'It's good to draw the line from the start and say no.' The opening phrase means 'from the very beginning', followed by a quoted 'no way'. Remarkably like English, Korean uses an idiom that literally means 'draw a line' for setting boundaries The word doubles the. Now let's listen to the whole office tour scene again.
이게 매일 아침 보게 될 시청률표야.
이게 우리한테는 성적표 같은 거지.
요새 칠 나오기 쉽지가 않아요.
되게 기대를 많이 하고 왔단 말이에요.
가끔 혼란이 오더라고요.
다들 내가 하는 거 잘 봐.
이번 주 개콘표? 없어요.
처음부터 안 된다고 선을 그어놓는 게 좋아.
You picked up the phrase for every morning, two meanings of the word for chart and ticket, and a crisp way to say 'there are none'. Next stop: lunch!
또 만나요!

lines.fragment: 그래서 되게 기대를 많이 하고 왔단 말이에요
다들 내가 하는 거 잘 봐
안 된다고 처음부터 확실하게 선을 그어놓는 게 좋아
